utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-95-13/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic and Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me begin by making sure that the audio equipment is working. Mr. Mrksic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Counsel for Defence and the Prosecution, can you all hear me? Thank you. I would call now for appearances. Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Paul Rogers appearing with Ms. Kristina Carey and our case manager today, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rogers. Counsel for Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone else in the courtroom. The Defence of Mr. Mrksic today will be represented by Mr. Miroslav Vasic, that is to say, myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, and everybody else taking part in these proceedings. Lead attorney Novak Lukic is representing Mr. Sljivancanin today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. As you are all aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that Status Conferences be held every 120 days for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the appellant an opportunity to voice concerns relating to his appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained person. The last Status Conference in this case took place on 19th June 2008. While Mr. Mrksic is presently in custody at the Tribunal's detention unit, Mr. Sljivancanin is currently on provisional release pursuant to a decision by the Appeals Chamber of 11 December 2007. Let me begin the core of the Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Mrksic's health. Mr. Mrksic, how are you doing health-wise? Everything is okay?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour. For the moment, everything is all right. Of course, given my age and my case history and everything, I had two heart operations but I'm keeping well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. I'm glad to hear that. Let me now update the case. I think the parties would benefit from that. The briefing for the appeals have now been completed, and public redacted versions of all the briefs have been filed, save for Mr. Sljivancanin's reply brief. However, it is my understanding that the counsel is looking into that, and I would ask him to file a public redacted version by the end of the day on Monday. Any problem with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Meron, we will abide by that deadline, and I was going to suggest that we do file it by Monday, and it will be. There was just a technical problem with respect to the two different computer systems and so on, but it certainly will be ready by Monday, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. Given the fact that briefings have been completed and this last public redacted version will be in our hands by the end of the day on Monday, I expect that the Appeals Chamber will schedule the appeal -- an appeal hearing shortly, for the second half of January, second half of January 2009. It is also my understanding that a confidential motion was filed yesterday by Mr. Mrksic pursuant to Rule 115 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The motion is incomplete, however, as it does not attach the additional evidence which Mr. Mrksic is asking the Appeals Chamber to admit. Therefore, I would request that Mr. Mrksic files a confidential addendum, a confidential addendum to his motion containing the additional evidence, and I would request that this confidential addendum be filed also by the end of the day on Monday. I see that Mr. Vasic has no problems with that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. There will be no problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we are all aware of the fact that the relevant Practice Direction grants the Prosecution 30 days to file a response to this type of motion. Now, in order to minimise delays, I would ask the Prosecution to file its response within 15 days of the filing of Mr. Mrksic's addendum to his Rule 115 motion, so that 15 days would start running from the end of the day on Monday. For the same reasons, I would ask the counsel for Mr. Mrksic to file his reply, if any, within seven days of the filing of the Prosecution's response. On this issue, I suppose, I do hope that neither the Prosecution nor the Defence for Mr. Mrksic have any problems with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had anticipated the opportunity to deal with the things in the fullness of the time available to us under the Practice Direction. Plainly, as the entirety of the materials upon which the Defence rely have not been filed with the motion, it's difficult to anticipate precisely how long it will take, but in the spirit of compromise may I ask Your Honour for 21 days in which to file? It's down from the 30, but it gives us that little bit of extra time to deal with things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You really think that you need that extra week?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I didn't think we needed it, I wouldn't ask for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay, you will have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm afraid that now Mr. Vasic will reciprocate by asking for some additional time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think I'll have any need to seek additional time. I hope that what my colleague files will be succinct and that I'll be able to respond within seven days, although he does have 21 days. But I do have another problem with respect to this issue, and that is additional evidence that I received from my learned colleagues and which I found in my locker just yesterday. So quite possibly, they could fall within the framework of Rule 115 as well, because I haven't had enough time to study them sufficiently, but they are additional evidence and testimony by witnesses who testified in the trial and that were of vital interest for the first instance judgement. Unfortunately, I received an announcement that there'll be more evidence waiting for me in The Hague. I received the announcement by e-mail in Belgrade, so it wasn't until I had arrived here that I was able to pick the material up. And I think I might find elements for applying Rule 115, which will mean that I need an extension of the deadline for my filing of additional evidence, because as I say, they were witnesses who were crucial witnesses at the trial itself in the first instance, and they were provided here, Your Honour, in another trial. So I don't know, given those circumstances, how the plan stands, the agreement we've just reached, in view of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So let me understand. You are talking about additional materials that you have received yesterday, and they are not in -- covered by the motion you have already filed, and they have been disclosed to you by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, you will -- you will, I'm sure, review these materials, and if you see that you have to file an additional motion, if they meet the requirements that you think that -- then do file that motion and we will review the motion. I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I am, to say the least, unhappy at the endless dragging of additional things at this stage, but if interest of justice requires it then so be it, and we will look at it. This does not affect the conclusions we have reached now. If there is another motion, we will establish what are the time limits that have to be applied to it, whether the regular ones or time limits that we would find it necessary to modify to speed up the process, but we will -- it's not yet, in fact, sure that you will find it necessary to submit additional motion, so there is no need to -- to proceed with that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I can just assist you with the nature of the material. It arises from the trial, ongoing trial in the case of Seselj, as I'm sure Your Honour appreciates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And we do, as Your Honour will remember from the last Status Conference, but there was an element of criticism for saving up witnesses to hand over to the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Excuse me. Before you proceed, are these confidential materials?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, some of them are. I'm not going to explain precisely what they.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I just wanted to warn you not to mention things in open court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not going to. I'm not going to mention any names, but simply just to explain the situation is that when we receive the information from the trial teams, we assess it as quickly as we can and we turn it over to the Defence as quickly as we can if it meets the criteria under the rules for disclosure. So there's no -- this isn't material we've been sitting on, if I can put it that way. It does go out as quickly as we can and as soon as we receive it, so that Your Honour understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: No, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I did not mean to attribute to you any kind of dilatory tactics. I'm simply worried about the results that we are faced with at the appeals stage with so many matters pertaining to Rule 115. When I tell my colleagues from other courts, say in the United States, that we have the 115, they say, "How can you -- how can you do that and deal efficiently with appeals while admitting additional evidence at this stage?" And I explain to them why we do need that. Still, it is something that does not make our task easier, and we are trying to -- to cope with that, and I do, because of that, appreciate the readiness of both parties to limit the time -- times which are stated in the Practice Direction. At this point, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Mr. Rogers, let me start with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Again in the spirit of informing all the parties for their best efforts to prepare, the Prosecution will not be pursuing subground (2), that's error 2 under ground 1. In light of the recent ruling in the case of Martic, the ground that relates to definitions of civilians that appears under ground 1, subground (c), on our brief, we will not be pursuing. Obviously the other grounds remain live, and we would invite, and I've spoken to my learned friends already, we would invite them, again in the spirit of defining the issues that need to be dealt with on appeal, to review their response briefs and file or notify the Court and us of any change to their positions arising from the Martic judgement. I'm sure they need little time to reflect upon that judgement, but it would assist everybody, including the Court in particular, if we were able to confine and define the issues efficiently and effectively, and I think it's over to the Defence now to indicate any changes in their briefs should they so wish to do. That's one issue. So far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Before you proceed, I would like to have some response as soon as possible from the -- from Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Lukic and I did consider the matter before coming to this Status Conference, and the Defence does have certain proposals which it would like to put forward, and Mr. Lukic will deal with the matter on behalf of both Defence teams, and he has written a motion on the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. So we will be getting a motion on this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll replace my colleague, Mr. Vasic. I was going to address you orally, but if you would prefer to have it in writing, that's what we will do. We'll follow your instructions. We did have a discussion, my colleague Mr. Vasic and myself, a moment ago before this Status Conference, and in light of what the Prosecutor has just said, it is obvious that the Martic judgement which -- the second instance which came several days ago and which deals with certain topics and has grounds for the Prosecution appeal, gives a new task to the Defence to look at these allegations in the first instance judgement. It was our proposal, and I can present it orally here, Your Honour, Judge Meron, and that is that the Defence be allowed, in light of the conclusions, the legal conclusions from the Martic judgement that the Defence be allowed to write an additional response to the appeal in writing, and we would like to have a 21-day time limit for that, and we'd be completely satisfied if we were to be allowed to use up to 6.000 words for that. And fully conscious of the fact that all the submissions have already been handed in which relate to the appeals, the replies and so on, that we be allowed to have additional time for oral arguments to be presented, and in them we would deal with what the precedent has to say in light of the second instance Martic judgement. So in that sense it would mean a lot if we could be given 45 minutes more time than the time specified for oral arguments so that we can state our views in respect of that and in respect of the Martic judgement. And I would just like to mention that both Defence teams are still studying the Martic judgement and we haven't defined our positions yet quite clearly, but in any case, I think that we would like to present additional arguments in light of the judgement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take the question of the supplemental document first, submission first. I would like on that a motion from you requesting that, because I may want to consult on that with my colleagues on the Bench, and I would -- I'm wondering whether you could have that motion, adjust that motion by the end of the day tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd be very grateful to you, Judge Meron, if you were to set the time for Monday, because my co-counsel is absent, but he will be here tomorrow. So may we be allowed to take until Monday, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes. I will -- in this case, perhaps by midday on Monday? Okay. With regards --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thanks. As regards the other question, namely of additional time for the oral argument, we will consider that in preparing the Scheduling Order. I think it's a bit early now, before I know what are the additional points you would like to argue, and it may very well be that if we allow a supplemental brief, that this will cover it enough. But in any event, I don't want to go into that now. When we prepare -- when we work on the Scheduling Order, we will take this question into consideration. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, as I see -- I see there is close coordination between Mr. Vasic and Mr. Lukic, so I'll -- I suppose they don't have any additional issues to raise at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, none. Thank you. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, forgive me, before you move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: There was just one other matter I wanted to raise with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I am terribly sorry. I did not come back to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Not at all. Your Honour, it's relating to the hearing date. Firstly, we're very grateful for the indication that you've been able to give so far today, but may I ask if -- because understanding the Tribunal's practice, certainly from the Appeals Chamber, to provide questions to the parties, such matters that concern the members of the panel that will be hearing the case, given the Christmas break that is approaching and to enable us all to effectively work through the period in order to prepare fully to assist the Court at the hearing, might I ask that the Scheduling Order come out in good time before Christmas with the questions that the Court wishes to raise so that the parties, not just ourselves but the Defence as well, can focus their resources, if we like, on -- on issues that are most troubling the Appeals Chamber? And I'm just conscious that if an order were to come very shortly before the Christmas period, those resources may not be best utilised. I'm sure the Court, wishing to ensure efficiency, will do its best to provide the parties with as much notice as possible to enable the effective preparation of the case for hearing. So might I invite the Court, if possible, to provide its Scheduling Order with its questions in perhaps the first week, if I may ask, of December or thereabouts so that we can prepare and allocate resources appropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Rogers, I have listened very carefully to your point, and I am -- I am receptive to the idea. We will do our best. If we cannot issue the Scheduling Order, including the questions, the first week of December, we certainly will do that during the second, as early as possible during the second week of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm very grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I think that we have exhausted everything which was on our agenda for this afternoon, and if there are no matters, and there are no further matters, I understand, that the Prosecution or the counsel for the Defence would like to raise, we will now rise and the meeting is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: at 3.26 p.m.
